apac3.notes:
# APAC third packet — 28 October 2026

Four proposed new commercial physical sites: SK Broadband Ilsan (Janghang), Siksa (Ilsan), Yangju and Pangyo. All retain the explicit operating observation of 27 August 2026, 62 days before this review. The source is the already admitted SK Telecom portfolio release. Its source ID, complete metadata and original raw bytes are reused without alteration. The previously admitted operator guide is also reused verbatim, although its compact source summary names only the first batch of centres; its captured body additionally supplies the Ilsan address.

Janghang uses the operator’s exact road address, Jungang-ro 1333, and parcel alias Janghang-dong 726. Its Google feature explicitly names the SK Broadband IDC and matches the parcel. Siksa uses the maintenance employer’s exact workplace at Sarihyeon-ro 101-11, corroborated by SK Broadband’s own dated careers posting naming the Siksa DC in Ilsandong-gu, Goyang. The two source points are 6,010.7 metres apart. They are two separate physical locations, not two buildings assumed to be a common campus.

The portfolio release calls these two locations “Ilsan” without street addresses. Mapping the Siksa centre to one of those two locations is an explicit identity inference from the operator’s own Siksa/Ilsandong-gu identity and the maintenance employer’s exact workplace. No numeric “Ilsan 2” alias is asserted because a primary source directly equating that numeric label with this address was not obtained. The employer advertisement is dated November 2025, and its unrelated current page elements are not used to refresh status. The August 2026 careers posting is identity evidence; hiring alone is not treated as proof of operation.

Yangju’s exact Ganap-ri 440-2 parcel comes from the city council. Its 2022 opposition resolution requested withdrawal but did not cancel the project. The city’s later December 2024 mayoral visit confirms continuity of the same SK Broadband development in Ganap-ri after a June 2023 permit. A planned February 2025 opening is not treated as achieved operation; the August 2026 release supplies that fact. The map point names the exact parcel address, not the data centre or a surveyed parcel boundary.

Pangyo’s public visitor landing page explicitly identifies the cloud data centre at Pangyo-ro 255beon-gil 46. SK Inc.’s financial statements confirm the completed transfer to SK Broadband on 1 July 2025. PDF page 91 (printed page 88) was rendered and visually checked. The admitted map point names the SK C&C host campus at the same exact address, so it is labelled a campus locator. It does not assert that every campus building is a data centre or identify an internal room. The older branding does not create a second site. This property is 7,974.9 metres from the existing SK Broadband Bundang IDC.

All four coordinates are direct native Google feature geometries, not search viewports or derived centroids. They are classified as community sources with unknown measured accuracy. Four map captures, six new primary identity captures and two reused primary captures support the additions. The full manifest also includes unsuccessful discovery paths and unused lead captures. Raw and metadata hashes are recorded; restricted copyrighted response bytes remain ignored local research files.

Centum remains on hold. The fresh operating statement is sufficient for status, but no precise primary facility address or parcel and matching named map feature was established. A district reference point and an unrelated SHINBINET/SUIDC address are not substituted. The failed English operator-guide retrieval and the municipal jobs pagination/search results are retained as discovery evidence only; the latter did not reproduce the relevant cached job row.

Deduplication parses all five baseline tables: 854 sites, 922 projects, 4,821 evidence rows, 231 imported source records and 231 identity mappings, plus 90 available hold/queued-change files. Korean country aliases, former operator names, local-language names and addresses were screened. Matches are the separate existing Gasan, Seocho, Bundang and Ulsan records; no duplicate of the four proposed sites was found. The source and mapping snapshots remain byte-identical in the dry run. Bounded later-status searches found no newer primary physical-state successor; dates remain fixed, and no part of the 318 MW future portfolio total is allocated to an individual site. The proposed SK Horizon establishment remains a future transaction.

The local build and deterministic validation produce 858 sites / 926 projects / 66 countries with ten new evidence records. Existing source metadata is reused. The only existing evidence changes are added project links or roles where the same evidence is reused. No tracked file, published snapshot, definition, source projection or configuration was changed by this lane. Americas independent peer review passed all 12 source hashes, 32 raw/metadata pairs, four locators and Siksa’s explicit identity inference. Its file path and immutable hash are recorded in peer-review-receipt.json.

# Americas pass 3 — 28 October 2026

Two additions against hundredfourth (854 sites / 922 projects / 66 countries): Elea POA1, Porto Alegre, and Tecto TFOR3 Mega Lobster, Fortaleza. No tracked files were written. Build and validate-only both pass to 856 sites / 924 projects / 66 countries and 4,831 evidence rows.

Elea's 9 September operator release explicitly reports present 24/7 operation. Its historical hold was location-only. The official 10 July 2024 gazette, page 203, TRF4 extract in the right column, explicitly identifies its cage at Datacenter POA1 - ELEA DIGITAL, Rua Engenheiro Afonso Cavalcanti 100. The rendered page was inspected. PeeringDB facility 11612 supplies the matching name, address, exact operator page and native facility point. The nested organization point in Rio is excluded. The nearest baseline site is Procergs, 3.85 km away. Tenant expansion since 2019 is not treated as a new building or opening.

Tecto's 24 August release explicitly identifies TFOR3 as the host of the Ceará National Data Centre environment. RNP's 25 August account reports the achieved launch that morning and availability of the hosted environment; Tecto's CRO describes hosting this infrastructure. The 25 August date is used as the latest corroborated observation of the existing commercial host, not a claim that all tenant workloads or planned capacity started that day. No university/institutional site is added separately. No planned or global MW figure is assigned as achieved capacity. The original inauguration was in October 2025, not 2026.

The Google feature is specifically named Data Center Mega Lobster - Tecto; its native coordinates are parsed at [0,1,0,14][9], with exact name at index 11 and place ID at index 78. PeeringDB facility 16578 explicitly gives the TFOR3 / Mega Lobster alias and same street. Its point differs by about 74 m and is not averaged into the selected point. PeeringDB campus 186 is a logical grouping: TFOR1/2 at Rua Raimundo Esteves 333 are approximately 2.5 km away. This grouping does not turn three dispersed facilities into one physical campus. Only TFOR3 is admitted. Baseline Scala Praia do Futuro is 1.23 km away and has a distinct name/location; no duplication found.

All five baseline data/identity/source files, every tracked holds file and available local changes/holds queues were searched. Historical POA1 holds in the thirtyfirst, thirtyfourth and fortyninth packets and the Tecto portfolio hold in thirtyfourth were explicitly inspected. Their location blockers are resolved only for these two facilities. The older Tecto hold's August TGIG1 date is not reused: the underlying body dateline is May 25, outside the window.

TGRU1 is held despite fresh 3 September primary physical-construction status. Its municipal plan supplies project identity, process number, merged glebas and the Bela Vista road but no published coordinate. The city-level Google result, unrelated ODATA/Equinix features, empty Nominatim query and DataCenterMap HTTP 429 are retained without claiming they locate the plot. No repeated blocked route or improvised centroid was used. Crusoe/Araico Iguazú AI has a 22 October primary proposal but only substation-adjacency location; it remains held. No forced third admission.

The capture manifest verifies 25 raw-response hashes, including supplemental leads and the retained HTTP 429 boundary. Ten source projections are admitted. Raw pages, maps and PDFs remain ignored local research artifacts; only factual projections are proposed for integration. Status dates derive from actual primary body/publication statements, never retrieval or generic update timestamps.

europe3.notes:
# Europe pass 3 — 28 October 2026

One qualified addition against hundredfourth (854 sites / 922 projects / 66 countries): CGE Data Center Konin, Poland. The bounded regional search did not force the requested candidate count. Hillwood Reguły and Sunly/Magnora Risti have fresh primary announcements but remain held for exact locator evidence. No tracked files, historical datasets or existing source bytes were changed.

The original Energa announcement visibly dates 3 September 2026 and describes a letter of intent for the planned commercial campus. It names Centralna Grupa Energetyczna and CGE171FF and forecasts first construction in early 2027. The admitted scope is the announced overall campus. The historical 18 May permit is kept solely as an exact project/investor/parcel bridge. Its existence does not justify a September permit observation or a claim that every later campus phase is approved. No commissioned MW quantity, operator, or legal ownership role is invented.

The canonical GUNB source cee-p1-gunb-rwdz-wielkopolskie is reused byte-for-byte at the metadata level. Its prior Beyond.pl summary remains untouched. The original archived ZIP hash and CSV member hash were independently recomputed; the three Konin case UA.6740.22.2026 rows identify CGE171FF and parcels 543, 544/1, 545/1, unit 306201_1, precinct 0010. The separate konin-permit-extract.json records those rows without designer names. ULDK returns these exact parcel identifiers and WGS84 polygons. The locator [18.2509149, 52.2535265] is a computed centroid inside parcel 544/1, verified by point-in-polygon and high-precision decimal arithmetic. It is labelled compiled_reference and a derived parcel-interior campus locator, with unknown horizontal accuracy. It is neither an authority-published point nor the full future campus boundary.

All five selected-base tables, published holds, local country holds and available satellite/coverage queues were scanned. No Konin site/project identity exists in the base. A bare 171ff match in evidence is an unrelated Keppel November URL token, not this investor; the queue hit is a Teraco JB1 East evidence UUID in South Africa. Both false positives were read individually. Prior Konin holds are the same lead; the dated primary announcement and official parcel bridge now resolve their specific missing facts. Supplier/city pages and bounded successor searches found no later primary cancellation, relocation, replacement or achieved construction observation.

Hillwood's initial unrestricted affine estimate was degenerate. Subsequent spatially constrained/SIFT trials still had only a handful of reliable controls; all estimates are rejected and retained solely to document the failed research route. Neither reguly-georeference.json nor the manually queried 562/4 parcel supports an admission. Risti's old map labels Sunly land, not explicitly the current data-centre plot; its regional SVG and adjacent electricity assets cannot supply the missing precise locator. The municipality's October 9 article reports an October 7 meeting, which is the event date to use if the locator is later solved.

Interlan's July 15 tender and Tet DC7's June 1 report are outside the window. Evecon Lihula has exact parcels but only July 8 initiation; generic October page updates do not refresh its status. These remain explicit holds. All new raw-response captures and metadata hashes are in capture-manifest.json; raw third-party bytes remain ignored local research. The no-write update build passes with 855 sites, 923 projects, 66 countries and 4,826 evidence rows.
